profile.note: Bogata w metale, ale bez lodu i węgla: woda i paliwo musiałyby przylatywać z innych ciał.
Dobre metale i słońce, brak lodu. Lepsza jako druga kolonia przemysłowa.
Ferryt i Silicyt, mało wody. Niska grawitacja nadaje się na wyrzutnię masy.
Pełny zestaw surowców T0 i atmosfera do turbin wiatrowych. Najprostszy start, ale droższy start promu z powierzchni.
Źródło wody i paliwa na później. Słabe słońce: energia z reaktorów.
Masywny dysk pyłowy Tau Ceti: Platynit i Ferryt z wypraw górniczych. Nie da się na nim budować.

stars.name: Sol (Sun)
stars.description: Our home star. A yellow dwarf star at the center of the Solar System.

stars.name: Proxima Centauri
stars.description: The closest star to the Sun. A red dwarf with a confirmed exoplanet Proxima b in the habitable zone.

stars.name: Alpha Centauri A
stars.description: The primary star of the Alpha Centauri system. Very similar to our Sun.

stars.name: Alpha Centauri B
stars.description: Secondary star of Alpha Centauri. An orange dwarf slightly smaller than the Sun.

stars.name: Barnard's Star
stars.description: The fastest-moving star relative to the Sun. A red dwarf 6 light-years away.

stars.name: Luhman 16
stars.description: A binary brown dwarf system. The closest known brown dwarfs to the Sun.

stars.name: WISE 0855−0714
stars.description: An extremely cold sub-brown dwarf. One of the coldest stellar objects ever observed.

stars.name: Wolf 359
stars.description: A red dwarf star, site of the famous Battle of Wolf 359 in Star Trek.

stars.name: Lalande 21185
stars.description: A red dwarf that is one of the nearest stars visible to the naked eye under good conditions.

stars.name: Sirius A
stars.description: The brightest star in the night sky. A blue-white star twice as massive as the Sun.

stars.name: Sirius B
stars.description: A white dwarf companion to Sirius A. One of the most massive white dwarfs known.

stars.name: BL Ceti
stars.description: A flare star red dwarf, part of the UV Ceti binary system.

stars.name: Epsilon Eridani
stars.description: An orange dwarf with at least one confirmed planet. A prime candidate for extraterrestrial life research.

stars.name: Lacaille 9352
stars.description: One of the brightest red dwarf stars in the sky, visible without a telescope.

stars.name: EZ Aquarii
stars.description: A triple star system of red dwarfs. Known for strong stellar flare activity.

stars.name: Procyon A
stars.description: The 8th brightest star in the sky. A subgiant star in the process of evolving.

stars.name: 61 Cygni A
stars.description: The first star to have its distance measured by parallax. An orange dwarf with a companion.

stars.name: Tau Ceti
stars.description: A Sun-like star with 5 candidate exoplanets, two possibly in the habitable zone.

stars.name: GJ 1061
stars.description: A red dwarf with three confirmed super-Earth planets, two in the habitable zone.

stars.name: YZ Ceti
stars.description: A red dwarf with three confirmed Earth-sized planets. YZ Ceti b may have a detectable magnetic field.

stars.name: Kapteyn's Star
stars.description: The fastest-moving nearby star after Barnard's Star. A halo star with 2 candidate super-Earths.

stars.name: Vega
stars.description: The second brightest star in the northern sky. A rapidly rotating A-type star with a debris disk.

stars.name: Fomalhaut
stars.description: Known as the Autumn Star. Has a massive debris disk and a controversial candidate exoplanet.

stars.name: Altair
stars.description: One of the vertices of the Summer Triangle. Rotates so fast it bulges at its equator.

stars.name: Arcturus
stars.description: The brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere. An aging red giant star.

stars.name: Pollux
stars.description: The brightest star in Gemini. An orange giant with a confirmed giant exoplanet.

stars.name: Castor
stars.description: A remarkable sextuple star system, with three binary pairs orbiting each other.

stars.name: Deneb
stars.description: One of the most luminous stars known. A blue-white supergiant hundreds of times bigger than the Sun.

stars.name: Betelgeuse
stars.description: A red supergiant and one of the largest stars known. Will eventually explode as a supernova.

stars.name: Rigel
stars.description: A blue supergiant and the brightest star in Orion. One of the most luminous stars in the galaxy.

stars.name: Aldebaran
stars.description: The red giant eye of Taurus the Bull. About 44 times the diameter of the Sun.

stars.name: Spica
stars.description: A binary system of two blue giants. The brightest star in Virgo.

stars.name: Antares
stars.description: A red supergiant star in Scorpius. One of the largest stars visible to the naked eye.

stars.name: Canopus
stars.description: The second brightest star in the night sky. A yellow-white supergiant.

stars.name: Achernar
stars.description: A blue-white star rotating so fast it is oblate. The brightest star in Eridanus.

stars.name: Hadar (Beta Centauri)
stars.description: A triple star system. A blue giant and one of the pointers to the Southern Cross.

stars.name: Acrux (Alpha Crucis)
stars.description: The brightest star in the Southern Cross. Actually a multiple star system.

stars.name: Capella
stars.description: A binary system of two yellow giant stars. The sixth brightest star in the night sky.

stars.name: Regulus
stars.description: The heart of Leo the Lion. A blue-white star spinning very rapidly.

stars.name: Adhara
stars.description: The second brightest star in Canis Major. A blue supergiant and the strongest UV source in the sky.

stars.name: Shaula
stars.description: A triple star system marking the stinger of Scorpius. A blue-white giant.
